title: $\omega_k$ is a primitive $k$-th root of unity
statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and set $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i / k} \in \bbc$. Then $\omega_k$ is a primitive $k$-th root of unity: $\omega_k^k = 1$, and no smaller positive power of $\omega_k$ equals $1$, so that $\omega_k^j = 1$ for a natural number $j$ holds precisely when $k$ divides $j$.
replaced:
$\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ is a primitive $k$-th root of unity in $\mathbb{C}$,
i.e.\ $\omega_k^k = 1$ and $\omega_k^j \neq 1$ for $0 < j < k$.
